text:
zoe: found another sneaky redaction leak in the electron sample app when using the renderer -> main IPC bridge + worker threads. request IDs end up in crash reporter payloads and pretty logs after a retry. repro below.

zoe: repro steps:
```
1) run samples/electron-telemetry with OTEL log hook + crash reporter enabled
2) perform an action that triggers a failing upload -> main process retries via worker thread
3) worker uses util.format to compose retry message and sends it over ipc: `ipc.send('log', util.format('retry %d req=%s', i, ctx.reqId))`
4) renderer/pretty logger prints the formatted string before the redaction hook runs in the main process, so reqId is visible in stdout and crash payloads
```

hugo: oh no. so IPC is carrying already-formatted strings that bypass redaction in the receiver. which side runs redaction? we run redaction as an OTEL hook in the main process only.

kevin: exact lines seen in console/crash payload: `Retry attempt 2 req=req-2334` and crash report metadata: `user_id:u7, request:req-2334`. structured telemetry shows req nullified but crash file + pretty output had raw id.

maria: that's different from previous runtime-level toggle gaps. root cause here is pre-formatted message sent across process boundary; redaction only runs on structured metadata or on final formatted string in the same process. IPC bypasses it.

zoe: suggested fixes: 1) avoid sending formatted strings over IPC; always send structured { msg, meta } and let receiver format/log so redaction runs there, 2) extend redaction to run in renderer crash-report pipeline before payload upload, 3) defensive: run a final small redaction pass in crash reporter and pretty printer (cheap substring check for "req=" then regex).

hugo: we should also update the sample's retry helper to use `ipc.send('log', { level: 'debug', msg: 'retrying', meta: { attempt: i, reqId: ctx.reqId }})` and have the main process attach the OTEL hook so it redacts. that keeps payload structured and consistent.

kevin: filed INC-5199: electron-ipc-preformatted-logs-leak-reqid - assigned devex.ops. I've added a short PoC diff in samples/electron-telemetry repo that switches IPC payload to structured form.

maria: parity note: desktop SDKs (electron/kotlin desktop) need a clear guideline: never send preformatted user-facing strings across processes if they include sensitive ids. treat inter-process messages as structured transport. adding to SDK parity doc.

devex-bot: :white_check_mark: Labels added: bug, telemetry, sdk-parity, samples-electron.

zoe: short-term mitigation: update crash-reporter upload to scrub any `req-` patterns from crash metadata before sending. I'll open PR with both mitigations: change IPC to structured + scrub crash payload.

hugo: also check Sentry attachments: we were serializing full pretty logs into Sentry breadcrumbs and those were ingested before redaction. need to scrub breadcrumbs or remove raw pretty logs.

kevin: PR opened: samples/electron-telemetry#7 - includes failing integration that simulates worker retry + asserts no raw req-* in stdout or crash payload. CI job queued.

maria: thanks. once PR merges let's add a short note in onboarding: "Electron sample: prefer structured IPC, avoid util.format across processes". will update quickstart checklist.

ops-bot: Incident INC-5199 updated: mitigation PRs linked and test added. ETA for patch: 2d.

zoe: final note: this one taught us a new class of leak (cross-process preformatted strings). please scan other samples that use IPC or child_process and flag any `util.format`/string concat patterns in logs. I'll run a grep after lunch. :coffee:
